title: Co-branding
slide_intent: Teach designers to identify who leads a partnership before deciding which identity a viewer should perceive as dominant.
strategic_value: Special Olympics can communicate whether it runs an activity or receives support from it by linking mark prominence and attribution text to the actual relationship.
demonstration: A decision column asks about the organizer, event title and partner roles. Two columns then distinguish Special Olympics-led work from partner- or event-led work.
practical_value: Establish who leads the activity and inspect the program title. Use those answers to choose the dominant identity and write a clear sponsor or beneficiary attribution.

content_islands.name: Co-brand introduction
content_islands.spec: State the importance of an appropriate hierarchy in red at left and identify the guidance as an initial assessment.

content_islands.name: Decision questions
content_islands.spec: Place the questions in the next column with checkboxes. Direct each situation to its corresponding option.

content_islands.name: Two hierarchy options
content_islands.spec: Align the two options at right. Describe the lead organization’s visual system and use examples of attribution copy to clarify the other party’s role.
